_meta.note: Resolved cases with published outcomes, expressed as rates (share of a population). Language models may already know these outcomes, so scores on them are optimistic. Add your own cases that happened after your models' training cutoff for an honest test.

fields.actual: Observed share (0-1) for the first outcome
fields.kind: action (people doing something) or belief (votes, opinions)

cases.source: UK Electoral Commission, EU referendum result 2016
cases.prompt: It is mid-June 2016. The UK holds a referendum on 23 June on whether to remain in or leave the European Union. Simulate UK adults who will vote. Outcomes: Leave, Remain. What share votes Leave?

It is September 2014. Scotland votes on 18 September on the question 'Should Scotland be an independent country?'. Simulate adults living in Scotland who will vote. Outcomes: Yes, No. What share votes Yes?
It is late September 2016. Colombia holds a plebiscite on 2 October to approve the peace agreement with the FARC. Simulate Colombian adults who will vote. Outcomes: Yes, No. What share votes Yes?

It is mid-May 2018. Ireland votes on 25 May on repealing the Eighth Amendment, which would allow the legislature to regulate abortion. Simulate Irish adults who will vote. Outcomes: Yes, No. What share votes Yes?

cases.source: Australian Bureau of Statistics, marriage law postal survey 2017
cases.prompt: It is September 2017. Australia runs a voluntary postal survey: 'Should the law be changed to allow same-sex couples to marry?'. Simulate Australian adults who return the survey. Outcomes: Yes, No. What share answers Yes?

cases.source: Pew Research Center, March 2024 (23% of US adults had used ChatGPT)
cases.prompt: It is January 2023. OpenAI's ChatGPT, a free AI chatbot, launched two months ago and is getting a lot of attention in tech circles. Simulate US adults. Outcomes: Yes, No. What share of US adults will have used ChatGPT at least once within the next 14 months?
